name: Nanyang Technological University
header:
Nanyang Technological University
Singapore · PhD in Mathematical Sciences; research MSc alternative with restricted/ad hoc intake
Selected Asia programme; no claim of a ranking cutoff.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• NPGS deadline 31 December 2026 precedes ordinary August 2027 admission deadline 31 January 2027.
• College of Science video essay is required; exact portal prompt and technical limits remain unknown publicly.
• Do not use the legacy application portal or its seven-day reference rule.
• UChicago English-medium waiver is plausible under central policy but needs School confirmation because
departmental wording differs.
• Current published advisor fit is strongest in representation theory and selected number theory; a broad
classical algebraic/complex-geometry group was not established by the reviewed roster.
• San Ling's VinUniversity leadership appointment requires supervision-capacity clarification.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct PhD admission accepts a mathematics bachelor's degree at Honours (Distinction) equivalent; a master's
is optional. UChicago mathematics is the appropriate subject, but NTU must assess grade equivalence.
International applicants are eligible. Research MSc intake is small and ad hoc; ask the intended supervisor
before treating it as a fallback. F-1 status does not confer Singapore residence or establish nationality. [s1] [s2]
[s26]
Before submission [Standing rule]
SPMS advises contacting a prospective supervisor before applying, including discussion of funding. Establish
degree equivalence and seek English-test waiver confirmation; prepare academic records, references, written
materials and the required science video. Select the scholarship route early: NPGS closes before ordinary
admission. Use the current portal. Medical examination and insurance belong to enrolment, not the initial
application. [s2] [s3] [s4] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact a prospective supervisor before applying, as SPMS advises. Prioritize Okada for p-adic representation
theory and Lim for modular representation theory; Chan for theta functions/number theory. Other listed
researchers have adjacent algebraic-combinatorics or quantum-topology fits. Current acceptance of new
students is explicit only for Okada; San Ling's outside senior appointment needs clarification. [s2] [s13] [s14] [s22]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use https://gradadmissions.ntu.edu.sg/apply/ linked by current NTU scholarship guidance. Previous portals are
expressly excluded. Current public instructions support reference-status checks and reminders, document
uploads, and online payment; FAQ allows additional document uploads after submission. No account was
created, no video prompt inspected behind login, and no reference invitation was triggered. [s3] [s4] [s8] [s12]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
August 2027 is explicitly identified in the current admission guide. NPGS dates explicitly cover AY 2027-28.
January 2026 stipend revisions are current public rates, not a promise against later changes. PGA remains
labelled AY 2026-27. Older SPMS amounts and mirrored GRE requirements must not silently replace the newer
central/divisional policies. [s1] [s3] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s9] [s10]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
August 2027: 31 January 2027, with applications opening 1 October 2026. Basis: the current guide explicitly
identifies August 2027 and gives the August 1 October-31 January calendar; no separate Mathematical
Sciences exception is listed. Exact closing hour/time zone is not stated. January intake uses 1 June-31 July; the
corresponding 2027-intake window has passed. [s3]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
NPGS AY 2027-28: 1 November-31 December 2026, exact hour unspecified. The NIE 30 December exception
does not apply to mathematics. Research Scholarship consideration accompanies admission; no earlier
separate mathematics date found. PGA public page still identifies AY 2026-27, so its 2027 deadline is
unverified. Yunqi lists no independent deadline. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Reference receipt [Conflict]
Current central rule: referees should complete reports within 14 working days of receiving the invitation. Its
relationship to the admission/scholarship closing date is not expressly reconciled with the all-documents
deadline. Arrange both before the applicable closing date. Central FAQ permits referees to contact the School
about late submissions, without guaranteeing acceptance. Ignore the obsolete portal's 7-day rule. [s3] [s4] [s11]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Upload applicable scores with the complete application by the relevant admission or NPGS deadline; no
separate later testing grace period verified. TOEFL/IELTS validity is two years, GRE five years. English
exemption must be resolved before relying on an incomplete test record. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Complete legible uploads and payment are due with the application; late documents are not normally
accepted. The School may request additional information later. NPGS applicants must meet its earlier date and,
if still undergraduates, obtain the required anticipated highest-distinction equivalence letter. [s3] [s5]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
The offer email supplies the individual acceptance deadline. No universal mathematics commitment date or
April 15 rule found. Admission processing may take four months or longer. [s2] [s4]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Departmental wording requires TOEFL/IELTS from international nonnative speakers; SPMS FAQ accepts TOEFL
iBT, with scores within two years, or IELTS. No current mathematics numerical minimum found. Central
admission instead conditions testing on the bachelor's medium of instruction. Seek a written School ruling on
that discrepancy. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
An English-taught UChicago bachelor's fits the central medium-of-instruction exception (inference), but the
department's broader nonnative-speaker wording and central case-by-case waiver FAQ prevent promising
automatic exemption. Ask spms-grad@ntu.edu.sg whether the transcript suffices or a Registrar
medium-of-instruction letter is required. [s1] [s3] [s4]
GRE General [Conflict]
Current Mathematics page: GRE/GATE optional; strong scores can help. SPMS FAQ strongly encourages GRE
and gives 319 combined verbal/quantitative plus 3.5 analytical writing as its benchmark. A mirrored older PhD
page says international applicants must submit GRE/GATE. Prefer the current divisional page but flag the
contradiction to SPMS. GRE validity five years. [s1] [s2] [s10]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
An older official PhD mirror welcomes, but does not require, the Mathematics Subject Test. Current divisional

PhD page does not restate a subject-test policy; submission value/handling for 2027 is unverified. It is not
established as required, forbidden, or disregarded. [s1] [s10]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload official transcripts for every university attended, grading/honours explanations, degree certificates
when available, and certified English translations for non-English records. Detailed marks are requested where
the institution provides them; UChicago's ordinary grading scheme should not be fabricated into numerical
marks. NPGS final-year applicants additionally need official confirmation of expected highest-distinction
equivalence. [s3] [s5]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
A separate detailed mathematics-content list is explicitly required for applicants whose degree is outside
mathematics or a closely related field. That special condition does not ordinarily apply to a UChicago
mathematics major. No universal separate mathematics-course spreadsheet was found. [s1]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
The non-mathematics-degree route requires course-content detail and an annotated list of independently
studied mathematics texts. No mandatory course-description attachment was identified for a mathematics
bachelor's; retain syllabi in case the School requests clarification. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Conflict]
Two academic references. Central guide requires institutional email addresses, while FAQ describes them as
strongly encouraged and allows academic or employer alternatives. For this applicant, two UChicago academic
referees with university email addresses avoid that inconsistency. [s3] [s4]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
NPGS and Yunqi each list two referee reports, not an additional third reference. Public pages do not establish
whether reports are shared automatically with admission, whether a separate scholarship invitation is issued,
or whether evaluation questions differ. PGA additional-reference mechanics are unverified. [s5] [s7] [s8]
What sends the invitation [Conflict]
Central guide says submission of referee details automatically triggers email. SPMS FAQ instead describes
invitations after the application is submitted. The precise current portal button/trigger is therefore unresolved;
warn referees before entering details. [s2] [s3]
Before versus after submission [Conflict]
Do not assume invitations wait for final application submission: central instructions indicate a referee-details
submission trigger, whereas SPMS describes post-application email. Check the current portal's send/save
wording before triggering an invitation. [s2] [s3]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The application portal displays reference-submission status and provides a Recommendations Page reminder
action. SPMS forwards the file for review only after the reports arrive. Public evidence does not identify a
guaranteed receipt-email message to the applicant. [s2] [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
No public current rule found for replacement of an already submitted letter, editing its content, reusing a
previous-cycle letter, or sharing it across scholarship/application records. Ask SPMS; do not assume the legacy
system's behavior applies. [s3] [s4] [s11]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Resume required by the central overview; cover academic and personal achievements, research
experience/skills, leadership and character. The lower checklist labels several supporting documents
conditional, so the overview is the safer instruction. No page limit, font, margins or file-size rule publicly
verified. [s3]
Statement of purpose [Unresolved]
No separately named mathematics statement of purpose beyond the central personal statement was
identified. Use the personal-statement field for academic development, research interests and goals; whether
the live portal adds a distinct SOP is unverified. [s1] [s3]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Central personal statement required: explain academic development, intended research and future aims
(faithful paraphrase). Public page gives no exact word/page limit or formatting specifications. No separate
adversity/background essay identified. [s3]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Research interests belong in the personal statement and applicable proposal. The public programme pages do
not supply a separate research-interest statement prompt or length limit. Discuss a suitable research direction
with the prospective supervisor. [s2] [s3]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
Central admission requires a proposal where applicable; ordinary mathematics applicability is not clarified
publicly. NPGS and Yunqi explicitly require one. Describe a developed research direction and motivation; exact
mathematics length, template, citation format and required level of specificity remain unverified. Do not
import humanities/communication word limits. [s3] [s5] [s8]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
No mandatory thesis or standalone writing sample identified for ordinary mathematics admission.
Research-publication abstracts are conditional supporting material. Optional thesis/paper uploads and link-only
acceptance are not publicly specified. [s1] [s3]
Publications list [Standing rule]
Provide research-publication abstracts if applicable. NPGS/Yunqi supporting lists include research publications,
but do not require applicants to have published. Neither public page specifies full-paper versus abstract
upload, separate bibliography format, or whether a URL substitutes for a file. [s3] [s5] [s8]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
For this mathematics major, no separate universal course-list writing task found. The special
non-mathematics-degree application requires course-content and self-study-text details; see
course-list/course-description entries. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
NPGS: proposal, CV and available research publications; no public extra essay questions or length
specifications. Final-year highest-distinction verification is an additional official document. Yunqi also requires a
proposal and two reports. Scholarship interview may follow shortlisting. PGA 2027 prompts and
shared-reference mechanics remain unverified. [s5] [s7] [s8]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
College of Science applicants must submit a short video presentation. Exact prompt, duration, file format, size,
and upload-versus-link mechanism are not public in the guide. Do not borrow the three-minute requirement of
unrelated NTU programmes. Applicants outside mathematics also submit an informal motivation essay; that
special condition does not ordinarily apply here. [s1] [s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
NTU Research Scholarship international PhD: S$3,000/month from January 2026, plus up to S$500/month after
qualifying examination, with annual tuition covered: S$36,000 or up to S$42,000 annually (12-month
arithmetic). NPGS international rate S$4,300/month = S$51,600/year plus tuition; benefits include conference
funding up to S$5,000 per financial year, S$500 annual books, S$1,500 one-time IT and S$600 thesis
allowance. PGA international rate also S$4,300/month plus tuition and up to S$3,000 annual conference
funding, but its page is for AY 2026-27. Yunqi lists S$3,000/S$3,500 before/after QE plus tuition. These are
award-specific rates, not guaranteed offers or additive stipends. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Research Scholarship: initial one year, renewable subject to progress and funding, maximum four years PhD or
two years research master's. NPGS/PGA: maximum four years, annual renewal/progress conditions. Yunqi: first
year then semester renewals, maximum four years. The PhD can last up to five years; a fifth funded year is not
promised. [s1] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
International eligibility [Conflict]
Research Scholarship, NPGS, PGA and Yunqi admit international applicants. NPGS/PGA require
highest-distinction-equivalent bachelor's performance; ordinary admission/Research Scholarship uses
distinction equivalence. Citizenship-specific external awards cannot be assessed from F-1 status. SPMS warns
MSc research support is generally unavailable, conflicting with central scholarship-level master's eligibility. [s2]
[s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
International awardees must fulfil Graduate Assistantship Programme teaching/laboratory duties; public award
pages do not state the mathematics hours. No post-graduation bond is attached to the listed NTU Research
Scholarship/NPGS/PGA. Continued support depends on progress and funding. Yunqi prohibits outside work or
concurrent awards without approval. Housing priority under NPGS is not a free-room guarantee. Enter
Singapore bank details before the 15th of the commencement month to avoid stipend delay. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Request Research Scholarship in the admission application; no separate form. NPGS is nomination-based with
its earlier application window and specified uploads; confirm the correct scholarship selection/workflow in the
current portal. Yunqi is selected in its Scholarship section and may require interview. PGA is nomination-based;
2027 application logistics remain unverified. [s4] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
The graduate scholarship directory lists additional awards including VinGroup and specialist industry/AI
schemes. Their nationality and research-topic conditions must be checked individually; pure mathematics fit is
not automatic. Prospective supervisors can advise on available project funding. Do not assume central
research-master's scholarship eligibility guarantees SPMS will fund an MSc place. [s2] [s25]
Application fee [Standing rule]
S$50 nett per research application, nonrefundable and nontransferable; pay by Visa/Mastercard before
submission. Unpaid applications are not processed. [s3]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
Automatic waiver is advertised for nationals of 56 listed countries who have resided there since birth; no
separate request is needed if eligible. The full country list is on the admission guide. Citizenship is unknown,
and UChicago residence makes the literal residence condition uncertain; ask whether temporary study abroad
is compatible before relying on it. No general hardship waiver verified. [s3] [s4]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
1. Representation theory / number theory
Emile Takahiro Okada
Representations of p-adic groups, character expansions, wave-front sets, Hecke algebras and
Langlands-related questions. [s13] [s14] [s15]
Nanyang Assistant Professor on current roster; homepage explicitly welcomes PhD applications.
Research evidence: 2026 · Types and stable wave front set of the theta representation
With Karasiewicz and Wang; Advances in Mathematics 503C, 111240. Current author paper list verifies subject and publication.
1. Representation theory / algebra
Kay Jin Lim
Modular representation theory, finite-dimensional algebras and algebraic combinatorics, including nilCoxeter
algebras. [s13] [s16]
Senior Lecturer on current roster; official-linked homepage, updated 20 October 2026, identifies current PhD supervision.
Capacity for a new 2027 student unverified.
Research evidence: 2026 · Simple modules for affine nilCoxeter algebras
With David Benson; author lists arXiv:2607.24247. Senior Lecturer title should not be confused with an inability to supervise:
current supervision is documented.
2. Number theory
Song Heng Chan
Theta functions, q-series, special functions and identities connected with classical number theory. [s13] [s17]
Associate Professor on current official roster; availability unverified.
Research evidence: 2026 · On Schultz's generalization of Borweins' cubic identity
With Heng Huat Chan, Zhi-Guo Liu and Wadim Zudilin; DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2026.110967. Publisher search extract supplies the
primary record; direct publisher fetch was blocked.

2. Number theory / algebraic combinatorics
Bernhard Schmidt
Character sums and cyclotomic methods in finite groups, difference sets and finite geometry; adjacent to
number theory, not a verified arithmetic-geometry supervision focus. [s13] [s20] [s21]
Professor on current roster; availability unverified.
Research evidence: 2025 · Semiregular relative difference sets related to Gauss sums and projective planes
With Ka Hin Leung and Tao Zhang; Designs, Codes and Cryptography 93, 5473-5485. Publisher verifies NTU affiliation; this
updates the older institutional bibliography.
3. Adjacent algebraic combinatorics / representation theory
Gary Greaves
Algebraic graph theory and combinatorics; a recent paper uses vertex operators, infinite-wedge
representations and symmetric functions in probabilistic models. [s13] [s18] [s19] [s27]
Assistant Professor on current roster; current PhD supervision corroborated by coauthor/student Haoran Zhu's homepage;
new-student capacity unverified.
Research evidence: 2026 · Vertex operators, infinite wedge representations, and correlation functions of the t-Schur measure
With Naihuan Jing and Haoran Zhu; author-submitted preprint dated 15 February 2026. Representation-theoretic fit is specifically
based on this work, not a claim of broad algebraic geometry.
3. Adjacent quantum topology / Lie theory
Andrew James Kricker
Low-dimensional topology, quantum invariants, skein modules and quantum trace maps; adjacent to
representation-theoretic interests. [s13] [s24]
Associate Professor and URECA Director on current roster; availability unverified.
Research evidence: 2026 · On 3d Quantum Trace Maps
With Qingjing Chen; author-submitted preprint dated 11 June 2026. Primary arXiv search extract read; direct abstract fetch was
disabled.
4. Adjacent coding theory; appointment caution
San Ling
Algebraic coding theory and finite fields. Historical number-theory/modular-curve interests should not be
treated as evidence of a current arithmetic-geometry programme; recent work includes algebraic-geometry
codes. [s13] [s22] [s23]
NTU roster retains Distinguished University Professor/Nanyang title; personal institutional homepage reports Senior Deputy
President at VinUniversity since July 2025. Confirm active NTU doctoral supervision before pursuing.
Research evidence: 2026 · Hermitian hulls of rational algebraic geometry codes and applications in quantum codes
With L. Sok and M. F. Ezerman; Designs, Codes and Cryptography 94, 194; DOI 10.1007/s10623-026-01939-2. Institutional
bibliography verifies recent subject.

text:
Nanyang Technological University
Singapore · PhD in Mathematical Sciences; research MSc alternative with restricted/ad hoc intake
Selected Asia programme; no claim of a ranking cutoff.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• NPGS deadline 31 December 2026 precedes ordinary August 2027 admission deadline 31 January 2027.
• College of Science video essay is required; exact portal prompt and technical limits remain unknown publicly.
• Do not use the legacy application portal or its seven-day reference rule.
• UChicago English-medium waiver is plausible under central policy but needs School confirmation because
departmental wording differs.
• Current published advisor fit is strongest in representation theory and selected number theory; a broad
classical algebraic/complex-geometry group was not established by the reviewed roster.
• San Ling's VinUniversity leadership appointment requires supervision-capacity clarification.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct PhD admission accepts a mathematics bachelor's degree at Honours (Distinction) equivalent; a master's
is optional. UChicago mathematics is the appropriate subject, but NTU must assess grade equivalence.
International applicants are eligible. Research MSc intake is small and ad hoc; ask the intended supervisor
before treating it as a fallback. F-1 status does not confer Singapore residence or establish nationality. [s1] [s2]
[s26]
Before submission [Standing rule]
SPMS advises contacting a prospective supervisor before applying, including discussion of funding. Establish
degree equivalence and seek English-test waiver confirmation; prepare academic records, references, written
materials and the required science video. Select the scholarship route early: NPGS closes before ordinary
admission. Use the current portal. Medical examination and insurance belong to enrolment, not the initial
application. [s2] [s3] [s4] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact a prospective supervisor before applying, as SPMS advises. Prioritize Okada for p-adic representation
theory and Lim for modular representation theory; Chan for theta functions/number theory. Other listed
researchers have adjacent algebraic-combinatorics or quantum-topology fits. Current acceptance of new
students is explicit only for Okada; San Ling's outside senior appointment needs clarification. [s2] [s13] [s14] [s22]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use https://gradadmissions.ntu.edu.sg/apply/ linked by current NTU scholarship guidance. Previous portals are
expressly excluded. Current public instructions support reference-status checks and reminders, document
uploads, and online payment; FAQ allows additional document uploads after submission. No account was
created, no video prompt inspected behind login, and no reference invitation was triggered. [s3] [s4] [s8] [s12]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
August 2027 is explicitly identified in the current admission guide. NPGS dates explicitly cover AY 2027-28.
January 2026 stipend revisions are current public rates, not a promise against later changes. PGA remains
labelled AY 2026-27. Older SPMS amounts and mirrored GRE requirements must not silently replace the newer
central/divisional policies. [s1] [s3] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s9] [s10]

Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
August 2027: 31 January 2027, with applications opening 1 October 2026. Basis: the current guide explicitly
identifies August 2027 and gives the August 1 October-31 January calendar; no separate Mathematical
Sciences exception is listed. Exact closing hour/time zone is not stated. January intake uses 1 June-31 July; the
corresponding 2027-intake window has passed. [s3]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
NPGS AY 2027-28: 1 November-31 December 2026, exact hour unspecified. The NIE 30 December exception
does not apply to mathematics. Research Scholarship consideration accompanies admission; no earlier
separate mathematics date found. PGA public page still identifies AY 2026-27, so its 2027 deadline is
unverified. Yunqi lists no independent deadline. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Reference receipt [Conflict]
Current central rule: referees should complete reports within 14 working days of receiving the invitation. Its
relationship to the admission/scholarship closing date is not expressly reconciled with the all-documents
deadline. Arrange both before the applicable closing date. Central FAQ permits referees to contact the School
about late submissions, without guaranteeing acceptance. Ignore the obsolete portal's 7-day rule. [s3] [s4] [s11]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Upload applicable scores with the complete application by the relevant admission or NPGS deadline; no
separate later testing grace period verified. TOEFL/IELTS validity is two years, GRE five years. English
exemption must be resolved before relying on an incomplete test record. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Complete legible uploads and payment are due with the application; late documents are not normally
accepted. The School may request additional information later. NPGS applicants must meet its earlier date and,
if still undergraduates, obtain the required anticipated highest-distinction equivalence letter. [s3] [s5]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
The offer email supplies the individual acceptance deadline. No universal mathematics commitment date or
April 15 rule found. Admission processing may take four months or longer. [s2] [s4]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Departmental wording requires TOEFL/IELTS from international nonnative speakers; SPMS FAQ accepts TOEFL
iBT, with scores within two years, or IELTS. No current mathematics numerical minimum found. Central
admission instead conditions testing on the bachelor's medium of instruction. Seek a written School ruling on
that discrepancy. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
An English-taught UChicago bachelor's fits the central medium-of-instruction exception (inference), but the
department's broader nonnative-speaker wording and central case-by-case waiver FAQ prevent promising
automatic exemption. Ask spms-grad@ntu.edu.sg whether the transcript suffices or a Registrar
medium-of-instruction letter is required. [s1] [s3] [s4]
GRE General [Conflict]
Current Mathematics page: GRE/GATE optional; strong scores can help. SPMS FAQ strongly encourages GRE
and gives 319 combined verbal/quantitative plus 3.5 analytical writing as its benchmark. A mirrored older PhD
page says international applicants must submit GRE/GATE. Prefer the current divisional page but flag the
contradiction to SPMS. GRE validity five years. [s1] [s2] [s10]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
An older official PhD mirror welcomes, but does not require, the Mathematics Subject Test. Current divisional

PhD page does not restate a subject-test policy; submission value/handling for 2027 is unverified. It is not
established as required, forbidden, or disregarded. [s1] [s10]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload official transcripts for every university attended, grading/honours explanations, degree certificates
when available, and certified English translations for non-English records. Detailed marks are requested where
the institution provides them; UChicago's ordinary grading scheme should not be fabricated into numerical
marks. NPGS final-year applicants additionally need official confirmation of expected highest-distinction
equivalence. [s3] [s5]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
A separate detailed mathematics-content list is explicitly required for applicants whose degree is outside
mathematics or a closely related field. That special condition does not ordinarily apply to a UChicago
mathematics major. No universal separate mathematics-course spreadsheet was found. [s1]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
The non-mathematics-degree route requires course-content detail and an annotated list of independently
studied mathematics texts. No mandatory course-description attachment was identified for a mathematics
bachelor's; retain syllabi in case the School requests clarification. [s1]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Conflict]
Two academic references. Central guide requires institutional email addresses, while FAQ describes them as
strongly encouraged and allows academic or employer alternatives. For this applicant, two UChicago academic
referees with university email addresses avoid that inconsistency. [s3] [s4]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
NPGS and Yunqi each list two referee reports, not an additional third reference. Public pages do not establish
whether reports are shared automatically with admission, whether a separate scholarship invitation is issued,
or whether evaluation questions differ. PGA additional-reference mechanics are unverified. [s5] [s7] [s8]
What sends the invitation [Conflict]
Central guide says submission of referee details automatically triggers email. SPMS FAQ instead describes
invitations after the application is submitted. The precise current portal button/trigger is therefore unresolved;
warn referees before entering details. [s2] [s3]
Before versus after submission [Conflict]
Do not assume invitations wait for final application submission: central instructions indicate a referee-details
submission trigger, whereas SPMS describes post-application email. Check the current portal's send/save
wording before triggering an invitation. [s2] [s3]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The application portal displays reference-submission status and provides a Recommendations Page reminder
action. SPMS forwards the file for review only after the reports arrive. Public evidence does not identify a
guaranteed receipt-email message to the applicant. [s2] [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
No public current rule found for replacement of an already submitted letter, editing its content, reusing a
previous-cycle letter, or sharing it across scholarship/application records. Ask SPMS; do not assume the legacy
system's behavior applies. [s3] [s4] [s11]

Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Resume required by the central overview; cover academic and personal achievements, research
experience/skills, leadership and character. The lower checklist labels several supporting documents
conditional, so the overview is the safer instruction. No page limit, font, margins or file-size rule publicly
verified. [s3]
Statement of purpose [Unresolved]
No separately named mathematics statement of purpose beyond the central personal statement was
identified. Use the personal-statement field for academic development, research interests and goals; whether
the live portal adds a distinct SOP is unverified. [s1] [s3]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Central personal statement required: explain academic development, intended research and future aims
(faithful paraphrase). Public page gives no exact word/page limit or formatting specifications. No separate
adversity/background essay identified. [s3]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Research interests belong in the personal statement and applicable proposal. The public programme pages do
not supply a separate research-interest statement prompt or length limit. Discuss a suitable research direction
with the prospective supervisor. [s2] [s3]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
Central admission requires a proposal where applicable; ordinary mathematics applicability is not clarified
publicly. NPGS and Yunqi explicitly require one. Describe a developed research direction and motivation; exact
mathematics length, template, citation format and required level of specificity remain unverified. Do not
import humanities/communication word limits. [s3] [s5] [s8]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
No mandatory thesis or standalone writing sample identified for ordinary mathematics admission.
Research-publication abstracts are conditional supporting material. Optional thesis/paper uploads and link-only
acceptance are not publicly specified. [s1] [s3]
Publications list [Standing rule]
Provide research-publication abstracts if applicable. NPGS/Yunqi supporting lists include research publications,
but do not require applicants to have published. Neither public page specifies full-paper versus abstract
upload, separate bibliography format, or whether a URL substitutes for a file. [s3] [s5] [s8]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
For this mathematics major, no separate universal course-list writing task found. The special
non-mathematics-degree application requires course-content and self-study-text details; see
course-list/course-description entries. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
NPGS: proposal, CV and available research publications; no public extra essay questions or length
specifications. Final-year highest-distinction verification is an additional official document. Yunqi also requires a
proposal and two reports. Scholarship interview may follow shortlisting. PGA 2027 prompts and
shared-reference mechanics remain unverified. [s5] [s7] [s8]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
College of Science applicants must submit a short video presentation. Exact prompt, duration, file format, size,
and upload-versus-link mechanism are not public in the guide. Do not borrow the three-minute requirement of
unrelated NTU programmes. Applicants outside mathematics also submit an informal motivation essay; that
special condition does not ordinarily apply here. [s1] [s3]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
NTU Research Scholarship international PhD: S$3,000/month from January 2026, plus up to S$500/month after
qualifying examination, with annual tuition covered: S$36,000 or up to S$42,000 annually (12-month
arithmetic). NPGS international rate S$4,300/month = S$51,600/year plus tuition; benefits include conference
funding up to S$5,000 per financial year, S$500 annual books, S$1,500 one-time IT and S$600 thesis
allowance. PGA international rate also S$4,300/month plus tuition and up to S$3,000 annual conference
funding, but its page is for AY 2026-27. Yunqi lists S$3,000/S$3,500 before/after QE plus tuition. These are
award-specific rates, not guaranteed offers or additive stipends. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Research Scholarship: initial one year, renewable subject to progress and funding, maximum four years PhD or
two years research master's. NPGS/PGA: maximum four years, annual renewal/progress conditions. Yunqi: first
year then semester renewals, maximum four years. The PhD can last up to five years; a fifth funded year is not
promised. [s1] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
International eligibility [Conflict]
Research Scholarship, NPGS, PGA and Yunqi admit international applicants. NPGS/PGA require
highest-distinction-equivalent bachelor's performance; ordinary admission/Research Scholarship uses
distinction equivalence. Citizenship-specific external awards cannot be assessed from F-1 status. SPMS warns
MSc research support is generally unavailable, conflicting with central scholarship-level master's eligibility. [s2]
[s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
International awardees must fulfil Graduate Assistantship Programme teaching/laboratory duties; public award
pages do not state the mathematics hours. No post-graduation bond is attached to the listed NTU Research
Scholarship/NPGS/PGA. Continued support depends on progress and funding. Yunqi prohibits outside work or
concurrent awards without approval. Housing priority under NPGS is not a free-room guarantee. Enter
Singapore bank details before the 15th of the commencement month to avoid stipend delay. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Request Research Scholarship in the admission application; no separate form. NPGS is nomination-based with
its earlier application window and specified uploads; confirm the correct scholarship selection/workflow in the
current portal. Yunqi is selected in its Scholarship section and may require interview. PGA is nomination-based;
2027 application logistics remain unverified. [s4] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
The graduate scholarship directory lists additional awards including VinGroup and specialist industry/AI
schemes. Their nationality and research-topic conditions must be checked individually; pure mathematics fit is
not automatic. Prospective supervisors can advise on available project funding. Do not assume central
research-master's scholarship eligibility guarantees SPMS will fund an MSc place. [s2] [s25]
Application fee [Standing rule]
S$50 nett per research application, nonrefundable and nontransferable; pay by Visa/Mastercard before
submission. Unpaid applications are not processed. [s3]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
Automatic waiver is advertised for nationals of 56 listed countries who have resided there since birth; no
separate request is needed if eligible. The full country list is on the admission guide. Citizenship is unknown,
and UChicago residence makes the literal residence condition uncertain; ask whether temporary study abroad
is compatible before relying on it. No general hardship waiver verified. [s3] [s4]
